name: Open a Country
description: Backend for the Open a Country skill, driven by Fluid's Country Atlas and written entirely through the Fluid CLI: open the country with `fluid countries open` (currency, mode, tax profile, 3-D Secure, legal settings, address fields and payment order seeded from the atlas), enable added languages with `fluid translations enable`, create the atlas agreements the user kept with `fluid countries agreements --create`, convert product pricing with `fluid countries prices` (preview, then write at the reviewed rate) or leave it inactive, translate the storefront into the market's languages with `fluid translations auto`, limited to the types the user chose, and QA the whole thing with `fluid countries status`, ending with the operating mode's launch checklist as the human to-do list. Expects a caller `context` with country_id, country_iso, currency_code, mode, entity_name, tax_name, tax_inclusive, requires_3ds, agreements_to_create, payment_integration_types, enrollment_fields, languages_to_add, theme_languages, pricing_choice, fx_rate, translation_scope, translation_types, launch_checklist.

steps.name: Open the country with the Fluid CLI
steps.prompt:
Open the country the user just confirmed with `fluid countries open`. The CLI seeds currency, mode, tax name and tax-inclusive pricing, tax invoices, 3-D Secure, legal settings, address fields and payment-method order from Fluid's Country Atlas; this step adds only what the atlas can't know.

Every write in this step goes through `run_cli` with `{ command: "fluid", args: [...] }`. Never write with `fluid_api`: Mist refuses `fluid_api` writes to `/api/settings/company_countries` and `/api/settings/languages`, and the CLI carries the checks (atlas seeding, already-open and already-priced skips, dry runs) that a raw write skips. `fluid_api` GETs are fine for reading. Put the full command before its flags (`countries open DE --mode otg …`), and run any command with `--help` if a flag is in doubt.

1. Read from the `## Context from caller` block above: `context.country_iso`, `context.mode` (`nfr` | `otg` | `usd`), `context.currency_code`, and, when present, `context.warehouse_id` (numeric; null when the user chose a NEW warehouse), `context.entity_legally_registered` (boolean; true only for OTG when they already operate in-country), `context.business_id` (their local tax/registration number) and `context.settlement_currency`.
2. Build the flags from ONLY the values present:
   - `--mode <context.mode>` (always)
   - `--warehouse-id <context.warehouse_id>` when it is a number
   - `--business-id <context.business_id>` when it is a non-empty string
   - `--entity-registered` only when `context.entity_legally_registered === true`
   - `--settlement-currency <context.settlement_currency>` when present
   Do NOT pass the tax name, tax-inclusive flag or 3-D Secure flag: the CLI seeds them from the atlas, and it sends a tax name only with tax-inclusive pricing (Fluid drops it otherwise).
3. Preview: `run_cli` → `fluid countries plan <context.country_iso> <flags>`. It changes nothing. Read `alreadyOpen` and `companyCountry` (exactly what `open` would send). If `companyCountry.currency` differs from `context.currency_code` (USD mode charges in USD while the atlas seeds the local currency), add `--set currency=<context.currency_code>` to the flags and run `plan` again until the currency matches.
4. If `alreadyOpen` is not `false`, the country is already open: do NOT run `open --reseed` (it would overwrite settings an admin changed). Record `already open` with its `companyCountryId` and mode; if that mode differs from `context.mode`, say so in STEP_OUTPUT as a human follow-up. Skip to step 6.
5. Otherwise open it: `run_cli` → `fluid countries open <context.country_iso> <the same flags> --yes`. Never pass `--reseed`. Don't pass `--legacy-defaults`: the create-agreements step creates the atlas agreements the user kept, so Fluid's generic country agreements and forms aren't wanted. `open` is idempotent: on an open country it changes nothing.
6. Verify: `run_cli` → `fluid countries status <context.country_iso>`. Expect `open: true`; read the `mode`, `currency`, `tax_name`, `tax_inclusive_pricing` and `requires_3ds` checks. For the warehouse, `run_cli` → `fluid countries list` and read the country's `warehouse`.
7. Report as STEP_OUTPUT (later steps need the id): the company_country id (`companyCountryId`), the country ISO, whether it was `opened` or `already open`, the exact `fluid countries open` arguments you ran, its mode, currency, tax name, tax-inclusive pricing, 3-D Secure and warehouse id, and every status settings check that is not `ok` with its `detail`. When `context.warehouse_id` was null and the mode is `nfr` or `otg`, flag that a warehouse still needs to be created.
acceptance: `fluid countries status <context.country_iso>` reports `open: true` with a non-null `companyCountryId`, and `fluid countries list` shows the country with a currency matching context.currency_code and a mode matching context.mode (case-insensitive).

The country was opened through `run_cli` with `fluid countries open <ISO> --mode <context.mode> … --yes` (STEP_OUTPUT names the arguments), OR STEP_OUTPUT says the country was already open and that nothing was reseeded. No `--reseed` was used, and no `fluid_api` POST/PUT/PATCH to `/api/settings/company_countries` was made.
The `tax_inclusive_pricing`, `tax_name` and `requires_3ds` checks in `fluid countries status` are `ok`, or STEP_OUTPUT explains each difference (for example an already-open country an admin changed).

When context.warehouse_id was a numeric id, `fluid countries list` shows that warehouse on the country; when it was null (new warehouse) for NFR/OTG, the STEP_OUTPUT flags that a warehouse still needs to be created.
The reported STEP_OUTPUT includes the company_country id (numeric or string, as the CLI returned it).

steps.name: Enable added languages
steps.prompt:
Enable every language ISO the user opted into in the Open a Country flow, with `fluid translations enable`.

Every write in this step goes through `run_cli` with `{ command: "fluid", args: [...] }`. Never write with `fluid_api`: Mist refuses `fluid_api` writes to `/api/settings/company_countries` and `/api/settings/languages`, and the CLI carries the checks (atlas seeding, already-open and already-priced skips, dry runs) that a raw write skips. `fluid_api` GETs are fine for reading. Put the full command before its flags (`countries open DE --mode otg …`), and run any command with `--help` if a flag is in doubt.

1. Read `context.languages_to_add` (an array of ISO codes, possibly empty) and `context.country_iso`. If the array is empty, report exactly `STEP_OUTPUT: no languages to enable` and STOP — that is a valid pass, not a skip.
2. Read the current state: `run_cli` → `fluid countries languages <context.country_iso>`. It lists the market's major languages with `enabled` and `languageId` for each.
3. Enable them in one call: `run_cli` → `fluid translations enable <iso> [<iso> …] --yes` with exactly the ISOs in `context.languages_to_add`. Do not add languages the user didn't pick. The CLI returns `{ enabled, alreadyActive, failed }`; languages already on are listed under `alreadyActive` and are not an error.
4. If the command fails because an ISO isn't in Fluid's language catalog (the error names close matches), record that ISO as skipped with the CLI's message, drop it, and run the command again with the rest — don't fail the whole step over it.
5. Verify: `run_cli` → `fluid countries status <context.country_iso>` and read the `language:<iso>` checks (or `fluid_api` → GET `/api/settings/languages`, `active_in_company`).
6. Report the enabled ISOs, the already-active ISOs, and any skipped or failed ISOs with reasons as STEP_OUTPUT.
acceptance: Either context.languages_to_add is empty and STEP_OUTPUT explicitly said `no languages to enable`, OR every ISO listed in context.languages_to_add now appears in GET /api/settings/languages with active_in_company === true (or as an `ok` `language:<iso>` check in `fluid countries status <context.country_iso>`), apart from ISOs reported as skipped with a reason.
The languages were enabled through `run_cli` with `fluid translations enable <iso…> --yes`, not with a `fluid_api` write to `/api/settings/languages`.
STEP_OUTPUT lists which ISOs were enabled, which were already active, and which (if any) were skipped or failed, with reasons.

steps.name: Create the country's agreements
steps.prompt:
Create Fluid's recommended agreements for this country from the Country Atlas legal templates the user opted to keep, with `fluid countries agreements`.

Every write in this step goes through `run_cli` with `{ command: "fluid", args: [...] }`. Never write with `fluid_api`: Mist refuses `fluid_api` writes to `/api/settings/company_countries` and `/api/settings/languages`, and the CLI carries the checks (atlas seeding, already-open and already-priced skips, dry runs) that a raw write skips. `fluid_api` GETs are fine for reading. Put the full command before its flags (`countries open DE --mode otg …`), and run any command with `--help` if a flag is in doubt.

1. Read `context.agreements_to_create` (an array of atlas agreement localIds, possibly empty) and `context.country_iso`. If the array is empty, report exactly `STEP_OUTPUT: no agreements to create` and STOP — that is a valid pass, not a skip.
2. Read the current state: `run_cli` → `fluid countries agreements <context.country_iso>` (no flags, changes nothing). Each atlas agreement comes back with a `status`: `linked` (already on the country), `inactive` (on the country but off), `exists` (a company agreement with the same title that isn't on this country) or `missing`.
3. Create them: `run_cli` → `fluid countries agreements <context.country_iso> --create --only <localId> [--only <localId> …] --yes`, with one `--only` per localId in `context.agreements_to_create`. Never drop the `--only` flags: without them the CLI creates EVERY missing atlas agreement, including ones the user opted out of. The CLI creates only `missing` agreements (never a duplicate title), scopes each to the country, sets its checkout flags from the atlas, and writes every atlas translation. One failure doesn't stop the rest.
4. Read the output: `created` (id, title, `translations`, `failedTranslations`), `failed` (localId + error) and the refreshed `agreements` states. A non-zero exit means something failed; still report what was created.
5. If any created agreement has `failedTranslations` (usually a language that wasn't enabled yet), run `run_cli` → `fluid countries agreements <context.country_iso> --translate --only <that localId> --yes` once for those localIds and record the result.
6. Report as STEP_OUTPUT: created (id + title + languages written), skipped (localIds whose status was `linked`, `inactive` or `exists`, with that status; an `exists` agreement needs a person to add this country to it in Settings > Agreements) and failed (with the CLI's error), with counts for each bucket.
acceptance: Either context.agreements_to_create is empty and STEP_OUTPUT explicitly said `no agreements to create`, OR every localId reported as created shows as an `ok` `agreement:<localId>` check in `fluid countries status <context.country_iso>` (or GET /api/agreements shows it, with a non-null id, scoped to the new company_country).

The agreements were created through `run_cli` with `fluid countries agreements <ISO> --create --only <localId>… --yes`, limited to context.agreements_to_create, not with `fluid_api` POST/PUT `/api/agreements`.
No duplicate agreement titles were created — anything already present was reported as skipped with its status, not re-created.
STEP_OUTPUT reports created/skipped/failed counts, and every failure (including a failed translation) has a reason.

steps.name: Convert product pricing (or leave inactive)
steps.prompt:
Apply the user's product-pricing choice for the newly-opened country with `fluid countries prices`: preview first, show the rate next to the ECB reference, then write at the rate the workflow found.

Every write in this step goes through `run_cli` with `{ command: "fluid", args: [...] }`. Never write with `fluid_api`: Mist refuses `fluid_api` writes to `/api/settings/company_countries` and `/api/settings/languages`, and the CLI carries the checks (atlas seeding, already-open and already-priced skips, dry runs) that a raw write skips. `fluid_api` GETs are fine for reading. Put the full command before its flags (`countries open DE --mode otg …`), and run any command with `--help` if a flag is in doubt. Never PUT `/api/company/v1/variants/{id}` to set a price: `fluid countries prices` is the only price writer here, because it skips variants that already have a price in the country, rounds to the currency's minor unit, never writes a zero price, and re-reads each product before saving.

1. Read `context.pricing_choice` (`"convert"` or `"leave_inactive"`), `context.fx_rate` (a number: the rate the user approved in the steps panel, units of the country's currency per US dollar), `context.country_iso` and `context.currency_code`.
2. If `context.pricing_choice === "leave_inactive"`, report exactly `STEP_OUTPUT: user chose leave_inactive; skipping.` and STOP — that is a valid pass.
3. Reference preview (writes nothing): `run_cli` → `fluid countries prices <context.country_iso> --from-country US`. Without `--rate` the CLI uses the European Central Bank's daily reference rate (or 1 when both countries use the same currency). Record `rate.value`, `rate.source` and `rate.date`.
4. Reviewed-rate preview (writes nothing): `run_cli` → `fluid countries prices <context.country_iso> --from-country US --rate <context.fx_rate>`. Record `from`, `to`, `rate`, `rounding`, `fields`, `variants`, `toConvert`, every `skipped` count, `activeAfterWrite` and the `sample` of before → after prices. Put the rate, the ECB reference rate from step 3 and these numbers in STEP_OUTPUT before you write. The ECB rate is shown for reference only; it never blocks the write.
5. If `toConvert` is 0, there is nothing to write: report the skipped counts and STOP.
6. Write at the reviewed rate: `run_cli` → `fluid countries prices <context.country_iso> --from-country US --rate <context.fx_rate> --write --yes` — the same rate and fields as the preview in step 4. Never pass `--overwrite`: a variant already priced in the country (`alreadyPriced`) or priced in another currency (`pricedInOtherCurrency`) stays as it is, so a rerun never converts a converted price. Don't pass `--activate`: converted variants keep their current on-sale state in the country.
7. Read the write's output: `converted`, `changedSincePreview`, `failed` (each with the API's message) and `refusedByPriceEditor`. A non-zero exit means some variants failed; the rest were saved.
8. Verify: `run_cli` → `fluid countries status <context.country_iso>` and read the `prices` check (and `on_sale` for the report; nothing on sale yet is a follow-up for a person, not a failure).
9. Report as STEP_OUTPUT: the ECB reference rate and the reviewed rate written, the rounding, and counts for converted / skipped (by reason) / changed since preview / failed, with example product ids for each bucket, plus the `prices` check's detail.
acceptance: Either the user chose leave_inactive and STEP_OUTPUT said so explicitly, OR STEP_OUTPUT shows a `fluid countries prices` preview (the ECB reference rate, the rate used, counts and before → after sample) taken before any write, and any write used `--rate` equal to context.fx_rate with `--write`, without `--overwrite` or `--activate`.

For convert with a write, `fluid countries status <context.country_iso>` shows the `prices` check `ok`, or the variants still without a price are accounted for by the reported skipped (noSourcePrice, roundsToZero, pricedInOtherCurrency), failed or bundle buckets; and a spot check of 3 products via GET /api/company/v1/products/{id} shows each converted variant with a variant_countries entry for the new country_id carrying a non-null price in context.currency_code.
No price was written with `fluid_api` PUT `/api/company/v1/variants/{id}`.
STEP_OUTPUT reports converted/skipped/failed counts, and no more than 10% of variants are in the failed bucket unless the failures are explicitly explained.

steps.name: Translate the storefront into the market's languages
steps.prompt:
Translate the storefront into the market's language(s), limited to what the user chose. The Open a Country skill showed the user what `fluid translations missing` reported per type and asked what to translate before this run started, because a workflow step can't stop to ask mid-run. Their answer is in context; never write a type they didn't choose.

Every write in this step goes through `run_cli` with `{ command: "fluid", args: [...] }`. Never write with `fluid_api`. `fluid_api` GETs are fine for reading. Put the full command before its flags, and run any command with `--help` if a flag is in doubt.

1. Read `context.translation_scope` and `context.translation_types`:
   - `theme` → theme strings only: `--type theme --type theme-sections`.
   - `all` → every type (no `--type` flag).
   - `types` → one `--type <type>` per entry in `context.translation_types` (names from `fluid translations types`, e.g. `products`, `categories`, `menu-items`, `theme`).
   - `skip`, absent, or `types` with an empty list → write nothing. Report exactly `STEP_OUTPUT: translation skipped (translation_scope: <value or absent>); nothing written` plus the command to run later (`fluid translations missing <iso>`, then `fluid translations auto <iso> --type … --write --yes`), and STOP. An absent scope means the user was never asked, so nothing may be written.
2. Determine the target languages: use `context.theme_languages` (the market's major languages from the atlas, e.g. `['es']` for Mexico). Fall back to `context.languages_to_add` only if `theme_languages` is absent. If the resolved list is empty, report exactly `STEP_OUTPUT: no market languages to translate; skipping` and STOP.
3. For each target ISO, read what's missing for the chosen types: `run_cli` → `fluid translations missing <iso> <the --type flags from step 1>`. Record `language.active`, `done` and each type's missing count.
   - `done: true` → already translated; nothing to do.
   - `language.active: false` → the language isn't enabled (the user opted out of enabling it). Don't enable it here; report it as skipped with that reason.
4. For each language with gaps: `run_cli` → `fluid translations auto <iso> <the --type flags from step 1> --limit 25 --write --yes`. Every `auto` call carries exactly the chosen `--type` flags (none for `all`). It machine-translates up to 25 items per type with Fluid AI and saves them; theme writes publish immediately. Repeat while the total `remaining` across types is above 0 and still going down, at most 8 runs per language. Items listed under `incomplete` or `failed` count toward `remaining`; pass `--skip <type>:<id>` for them on later runs so they aren't retried.
   - If `auto` refuses because the ISO is the store's default language, that language is the source text, not a translation: report it as `store default language` and move on.
5. Run `fluid translations missing <iso> <the same --type flags>` again for every language you translated.
6. Report as STEP_OUTPUT: the user's choice (`translation_scope` and `translation_types`), the exact arguments of every `fluid translations auto` call, and per language and per type: already-translated / translated-now (count) / remaining (count) / failed (with the CLI's reason), plus any skipped language with its reason. When work remains after 8 runs, give the command to finish it.
acceptance: STEP_OUTPUT records the user's choice from context.translation_scope (and context.translation_types for `types`). When the scope was `skip` or absent, STEP_OUTPUT says nothing was written and no `fluid translations auto --write` ran.

Every `fluid translations auto … --write` call listed in STEP_OUTPUT carries only the types the user chose (`--type theme --type theme-sections` for `theme`, no `--type` for `all`, exactly context.translation_types for `types`) — no other type was written.

The step targeted the market languages from context.theme_languages (falling back to languages_to_add) — NOT an empty set just because no new languages were enabled. If the resolved target list was genuinely empty, STEP_OUTPUT said so explicitly.

For every target language translated, STEP_OUTPUT reports the `fluid translations missing <iso>` result before and after for the chosen types, with per-type translated-now / remaining / failed counts backed by the CLI's JSON — no invented success. When theme strings were chosen, GET /api/v202604/themes/active, then GET /api/application_themes/{id}/resources, shows a `locales/<iso>.json` with non-blank values for each language reported as translated.

steps.name: Final QA + launch checklist
steps.prompt:
Verify the whole Open a Country flow holistically, then hand the user their launch checklist. Every verification claim you make MUST be backed by a read performed THIS turn — do not trust the earlier steps' summaries. This step writes nothing: no `fluid_api` writes and no `fluid` command that changes anything (`open`, `--create`, `--translate`, `--write`, `enable`).

Write the entire report in plain language for a non-technical store owner: NO internal identifiers (translate ids into what they are — "the Mexico store", "the Spanish privacy policy", "3 of your 5 products"), and no jargon like "STEP_OUTPUT", "company_country", or "acceptance criteria". Describe what's set up and what they still need to do, not the checking you did.

1. `run_cli` → `fluid countries status <context.country_iso>`. This is the backbone: it compares the country with the atlas (mode, currency, tax name, tax-inclusive pricing, 3-D Secure, tax invoices, payment order, legal settings, address fields), checks that every variant of the active products has a price there and something is on sale, and checks each market language and atlas agreement. Confirm `open: true` and read every check that is not `ok`.
2. Agreements: confirm every agreement the create-agreements step reported as created shows as an `ok` `agreement:<localId>` check (on the country, active, with every atlas translation). Fall back to `fluid_api` → GET `/api/agreements` if you need the titles.
3. Pricing:
   - If `context.pricing_choice === "convert"`: the `prices` check should be `ok`. Converted variants keep their on-sale state, so if `on_sale` isn't `ok`, list putting products on sale in the country as a follow-up rather than a failure. Also spot-check 3 products via `fluid_api` → GET `/api/company/v1/products/{id}`: their variants should have a `variant_countries` row for the new country with a non-null local price.
   - If `context.pricing_choice === "leave_inactive"`: spot-check 3 products via GET `/api/company/v1/products/{id}` and confirm their variants do NOT have an active country row for the new country (or that any auto-created rows are `active: false`).
4. Languages: confirm every ISO in `context.languages_to_add` has an `ok` `language:<iso>` check (or `active_in_company === true` in GET `/api/settings/languages`).
5. Storefront language: report what the user chose to translate (`context.translation_scope`, and `context.translation_types` for specific types). For each ISO in `context.theme_languages` (fallback `context.languages_to_add`), run `run_cli` → `fluid translations missing <iso>` (it only reads) and report `done` and what's still untranslated per type. This is the check that catches a Spanish market shipped with an English-only storefront — call it out loudly in the summary if a market language is missing from the theme.
6. `fluid_api` → GET `/api/payment_integrations` and compare against `context.payment_integration_types`: list which of the user's chosen methods are already configured and which still need onboarding in Payments settings. This is a report, not a write — payment integrations need credentials only a human can supply.
7. If `context.enrollment_fields` is non-empty, note them as a follow-up: the enrollment form for this country should carry those fields (id, label, component). Do not attempt to build the form yourself.
8. Produce the ready-to-launch report in two parts:
   a. **Setup verification** — what's confirmed, what's missing or degraded (every status check that isn't `ok`, in plain words), follow-ups from steps 6-7 (payment onboarding gaps, enrollment form fields, test mode, bundles to price by hand), plus any converted-price or translated-copy review notes.
   b. **Launch checklist** — render `context.launch_checklist` (the atlas checklist for the user's operating mode) as a numbered to-do list, each item's label bold with its description underneath, VERBATIM from the context — these are per-market compliance obligations (registrations, licenses, filings); do not summarize, reorder, or drop any.
acceptance: The summary explicitly covers: country existence (with tax profile), agreements created, pricing outcome (converted or intentionally inactive), language enablement, storefront translation status (including what the user chose to translate), and payment-integration gaps.

Every verification claim is backed by a read performed in this turn (`fluid countries status`, `fluid translations missing`, or a `fluid_api` GET) — no claim rests only on trust of earlier STEP_OUTPUT lines.
The launch checklist from context.launch_checklist is reproduced in full — same item count, labels and descriptions intact.
